correctness.rationale: For each plant, extinction probability is binom(v-d,s)/binom(v,s); for each plant pair with common-neighbor number t, joint extinction is binom(v-2d+t,s)/binom(v,s). Indicator covariance gives the stated exact variance. Biregularity makes the average t equal one; Pascal differences give convexity for all m and strict support at t=1 for 2d-2<=m<=v-2. Equality requires all t=1, equivalent to a symmetric (v,d,1) point-line design. Finite fields provide such designs for all prime powers. At the first stage m=2d-2, two plants vanish simultaneously iff a pair has overlap at least two. Exact checks of all deletion subsets for prime orders two and three and symbolic identities through seven confirm example arithmetic, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The assessed contribution is a sharp simultaneous variance-minimization and coextinction-cluster suppression theorem under fixed two-sided degrees. The primary 2004 model and the 2024 mean-optimality result do not imply the variance comparison; a 7-by-7 degree-three edge switch preserves the entire mean curve but changes four-loss variance from 4/25 to 48/175. Known projective planes are used, not newly constructed. A related variance paper with a stochastic-block-model objective had abstract-only access, so remaining overlap uncertainty is expressly documented.
residual_risks: Full text of Chabert-Liddell et al. (arXiv:2106.06348 / DOI 10.1002/env.2709) was inaccessible; its exact propositions could contain related optimizers.
Classical reliability or combinatorial-design sources could independently contain an equivalent fixed-size coverage-variance convexity extremum.
The result concerns a special regular ecological network class and should not be generalized to biological field networks without further evidence.

value.rationale: Jones et al. explicitly identify secondary-extinction standard deviation as a further analytic target. This theorem gives a complete infinite-family design solution at every random-loss stage, plus a deterministic sharp no-two-coextinctions threshold and an exact positive variance gap. The q=2 equal-mean/different-variance witness confirms material information not captured by existing mean robustness results. The exact restricted problem is ecologically motivated even without implying field-level management prescriptions.
